label: Isometry fails within a species
statement_en: areaExponent < 2 and 1 < wingLoadingExponent, with the mass exponent in [2.90, 3.02].

hypotheses.name: Delphi.Empirical.WithinSpeciesAllometry
hypotheses.statement: areaExponent < 2 and 1 < wingLoadingExponent, with the mass exponent in [2.90, 3.02].

entries.note: the abstract calls growth in mass negatively allometric; 2.981 is just below the isometric 3

entries.quantity: lateral fin area vs standard length
entries.note: below the isometric 2: fins grow relatively smaller as the fish grows

hypotheses.source: physics/allometry.json (Davenport 1992, as the physics thread recorded it)
hypotheses.observation: Within one species, pectoral fin area grows as SL^1.834 and wing loading as SL^1.236 (mass as SL^2.981): fin area falls behind the isometric square and wing loading outruns the isometric first power, so a bigger fish of the same species is more heavily loaded than isometry predicts.

scope.basis: Davenport 1992 (physics/allometry.json): within-species regressions on Exocoetus obtusirostris
scope.note: Three separate regressions, no confidence intervals, and NOT mutually consistent: 2.981 - 1.834 = 1.147 against the fitted 1.236. That inconsistency is why C13 needs intervals, and it is the reason nine audit rows read "violated" rather than a defect of those theorems.

areaExponent.description: log-log slope of lateral/pectoral fin area on standard length (within species)

wingLoadingExponent.description: log-log slope of wing loading on standard length (within species)

massExponent.description: log-log slope of body mass on body length (fitted)
